Title: Payday Double Dice - Super Mario Wiki
URL: https://www.mariowiki.com/Payday_Double_Dice
Published: N/A
Author: N/A
Highlights:
The Payday Double Dice is an item in Super Mario Party Jamboree. It looks like a Double Dice but is completely plated in solid gold. It acts identically to a Double Dice with the player rolling two Dice Blocks. However, when the total roll is revealed, the player will then receive coins equal to the amount rolled, much like the Plus Block from the first Mario Party. The player can potentially get 2-20 free coins with the Payday Double Dice, along with an additional 10 coin bonus for matching numbers similar to the Double Dice. It has a Triple Dice variant in the Payday Triple Dice. 

Mario's Jamboree Buddy ability dice roll also adds to the total amount of coins for a maximum of 38 coins (with a roll of matching tens for 20 coins, the 10 coin bonus, and an 8 from Mario). 

This item is purchasable in Rainbow Galleria's Golden Shop, and on other boards, they're normally found in Item Shops for 10 Coins (5 during a flash sale or if the player has Daisy as a Jamboree Buddy, or 20 if the player is under the effect of a Markup Sticker) after shop inventories have been updated half way into a match. The one exception is Kamek's Shop on Western Land, which sells Payday Double Dice from the start. It is also one of the dice items that can be randomly obtained from paying 10 coins at the Dice Shop pit stop on Roll 'em Raceway. It can also be obtained from an Item Space.

- If bought for the regular price of 10 coins, the Payday Double Dice have a 68% chance of paying for themselves — a 64% chance of rolling at least a 10 (as noted on the Double Dice page) and a 4% chance of rolling a double 1-4 for a 10 coin bonus.

Jamboree Buddies are characters who assist a character in Super Mario Party Jamboree, with 10 of the 22 playable characters having this role. When a character encounters a Jamboree Buddy on the board, a Showdown minigame linked to the Jamboree Buddy begins, wherein the character who activates it has a slight advantage at the start. If a tie occurs, the player who rolls the highest in the following "Tie-Break Dice" event earns the Jamboree Buddy.

Title: Super Mario Party Jamboree - Super Mario Wiki, the Mario encyclopedia

Published: 2026-07-10T00:00:00.000Z
Author: N/A
Highlights:
Like with its predecessor, Super Mario Party Jamboree features the traditional Mario Party gameplay as the main mode of the game; players traverse a game board to collect coins in order to purchase Stars. The gameplay is overall more similar to Mario Party Superstars than Super Mario Party, sharing many of the same rules and mechanics, such as the dice rolling between one and ten and the occurrence of Bonus Minigames, where the coins won are doubled. Various new mechanics are introduced, including Jamboree Buddies, allies that grant the player a unique ability and trigger a space's effect twice upon landing, which serve as a revamped version of the ally mechanic from Super Mario Party. When a player passes by an unaffiliated Jamboree Buddy on the board, all players participate in a Showdown minigame, where the one who passed them is granted a slight advantage and the winner recruits the Jamboree Buddy.

Title: What Does Each Jamboree Buddy Do In Super Mario Party Jamboree?
URL: https://www.thegamer.com/super-mario-party-jamboree-buddy-allies-abilities-minigames-perks/
Published: 2024-10-23T15:30:17.000Z
Author: Gabrielle Castania
Highlights:
Like their minigames, each character in Super Mario Party Jamboree has a unique buddy ability to help the player they’re following get ahead in some way. This can be by gifting you free coins or items, cutting the prices of items at shops, helping you roll higher numbers, and more. You’ll receive some kind of buddy perk at the start of your turn for the entire duration your buddy is by your side, which we will detail more below.

Not only do you get the unique perk for each of the ten characters available as buddies in the game, but you’ll also have the option to buy two items when you have a buddy with you. This includes things like stars, items from stores around the game board, and requests for Boo to steal from your opponents, so it’s helpful to pop by one of these locations when you have a buddy with you.

The list of things that double when you have a Jamboree Buddy in Super Mario Party Jamboree are:

- Blue and Red Spaces, meaning you'll receive six coins or lose six coins total on that turn. 
- Lucky and Unlucky Spaces, which make you stop that space's spinner twice. 
- Item Shops will sell you a second item when you stop by with a Jamboree Buddy. 
- Star Spaces will sell you two stars instead of one, provided you've got the money to afford both. 
- Boo will steal from your opponents twice in one stop by any given Boo space.

Each Jamboree Buddy grants the user a unique ability or bonus, so there are many ways to devise strategies around the Buddy mechanic. Mario increases your dice roll's final number by up to 8 points, so it's worth using special dice and other items while you're working hand-in-hand with the Italian plumber.
If you're trying to reach a star or other point of interest around the board, then Mario is one of the best Jamboree Buddies to have on your side. If you don't have any special dice but you happen to gain Mario as a friend, then at least you'll still have a slightly better dice roll than usual.

With Pro Rules, the Lucky Space has undergone an exciting transformation. You can now choose your reward for landing on a Lucky Space - a Double Dice or 10 coins. Double Dice only cost 5 coins to buy, so you're better off taking the 10 coins and then buying a Double Dice in the shop.
As long as Double Dice isn't sold out yet, the extra coins will always be the better option since you'll get an extra 5 on top of the special dice. Now, you can use your new coins to buy a second item or put them toward a star.

Gaining a Jamboree Buddy comes with a ton of benefits, but perhaps the most useful feature is the ability to perform certain actions twice. You can buy two stars when you have a Jamboree Buddy, and Princess Peach cuts the price of stars in half if she's following you.
If you can, try to get to a star while you have a Jamboree Buddy so that you can double your reward. It's also a good idea to save special dice and other items if you think you can secure a follower during your current match.
